title: Choose the visual world for Team Liquid ID
question: Four genuinely different worlds. The roll assigned the contact sheet; the rest are real alternates. Pick the one worth building the whole site around.

options.label: The Selects
options.lineage: darkroom contact sheets of match moments
options.thesis: The team is the strip of moments that survives the cut, not the roster on a page.
options.viewport: A full-width contact strip of numbered match frames; the newest frame carries a folded tape flag and a grease-pencil mark.
options.risk: Can read as an archive gallery unless the current pulse is unmistakably live.

raised.raise: Pulse copy stacks in three fixed tiers: hook, current state, stakes.
Each frame carries one hand-drawn annotation ribbon naming the player and the moment.
One continuous strip with a single travelling highlight marks the live position.
State is a mark, not a hue: flag, cross, punch, or hang.

options.label: The Draw
options.thesis: The team exists as one line in a larger bracket, printed fresh each round.
options.viewport: A ruled front page whose bracket lines are the page grid, with today's edition marked in vermilion.
options.risk: The most familiar editorial direction in this category; it must be set with real conviction.

options.label: The Loom
options.thesis: Every match is a row of thread decisions resolving into one pattern.
options.viewport: A woven ground where a punch-card row becomes the live pulse and player statistics surface as gold floats.
options.case: Fuses strongly: the binary matrix gives statistics a native, legible form. Holds product clarity, loses casual fan identification.
options.risk: The loom metaphor can bury a first-time visitor under instruction rows.

options.label: The Overprint
options.thesis: Two inks, slightly out of register, print the team as a living sheet.
options.viewport: A paper-toned page where a fluorescent now-band and spot-coloured index rail carry the pulse and navigation.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: spot inks map to sections and the misregister hover is cheap CSS. Holds product clarity, loses fan-world identification.
options.risk: Can read as a design-studio template if the ink layers stay decorative instead of structural.

options.label: The Rack
options.thesis: Each player turns face-out from a spinning rack of painted promises.
options.viewport: A carousel of player covers with one turned face-out and three tiers of cover lines.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a rack of lurid covers obscures the live pulse and hides competitive facts.
options.kept: Three-tier cover-line hierarchy, donated to the assigned direction's pulse copy.

options.label: The Mook
options.thesis: Hand-drawn ribbons annotate every detail of a shingled player spread.
options.viewport: Shingled player photographs with unfurling ribbon captions and a folded sheet in the gutter.
options.case: Fuses thinly: the annotation grammar belongs to garments, and casual fans do not identify with this subculture.
options.kept: The annotation-ribbon discipline, donated to the assigned direction's frame labels.

options.label: The Circuit
options.thesis: The team name is one continuous glass run that ignites from within.
options.viewport: A single continuous bent-glyph word with the active run lit and the circuit breaks named.
options.case: Fuses poorly: electrode and transformer topology maps weakly to team facts and risks the dark-with-glow convention the brief rejects.
options.kept: One continuous run with a single active highlight, donated to the assigned strip.

options.label: The Bench
options.thesis: The season is a perforated rail of frames, flagged where the editor stopped.
options.viewport: A perforated strip snapping between frames with a folded tape flag at the current position.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a cutting bench is a tool an operator uses, not a world a fan inhabits.
options.kept: State as a mark rather than a hue, donated to the assigned direction.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The conventional esports landing page, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A hero with the team photo, a roster card row, a fixture list, and a stat panel.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every competitor by design.
